desc: Finalize characterization: answer = min over (a) shortest closed walk from S through T containing a cycle, (b) tree-branch passing gadget walks; -1 iff graph is a path.
Design O(N+M) algorithm: BFS from S and T; detect whether graph is a path; compute min cycle-closed-walk via edge scan; compute branch-gadget cost for tree-like cases.
Verify formulas by hand on samples (3, -1, 4) and custom cases.
Stress-test current solution vs brute-force BFS; identified concrete failures: C4 S=1,T=3 (true 4, code outputs 6) and junction-beyond-endpoint cases.

Derive correct unified formula: candidate A (common cycle) = min over edges of (ds[x]+dt[y]+1)+(ds[y]+dt[x]+1); candidate B (theta) = min over edges of ds[x]+dt[y]+dt[x]+ds[y]+2; candidate C (junction) = 2*(ds[v]+dt[v])+2 (+2 if v∈{S,T}). Verified C4 gives 4 via candidate A.
Implement corrected O(N+M) algorithm with the three candidates and stress-test against brute-force BFS on all graphs N≤6 to validate.
Final stress-test validation on random graphs N≤8 and edge cases (path graphs, stars, complete graphs).
